blocks.body: The controls on a handheld are jobs, not decorations. Power runs the radio. Volume is how loud the speaker is. The big number is the frequency it is set to.

Squelch closes the speaker when nothing is stronger than its setting. It does not make a weak signal clearer. A VFO is the frequency you are tuning freely. A memory is a saved frequency you can recall.
Operate the radio for each step. The checklist counts only what the controls actually do.

tasks.prompt: Raise the volume until it is at least 3 of 9.
Stay off the strong signal and raise squelch until the background noise closes.
From 146.520 MHz, move the VFO up by 100 kHz.

tasks.label: 146.520 MHz
tasks.prompt: Return the VFO to 146.520 MHz and store it in a memory channel.

tasks.label: 146.520 MHz
tasks.prompt: Switch to the VFO and tune at least 50 kHz away from the stored frequency.

tasks.label: 146.520 MHz
tasks.prompt: Recall the memory so the display shows 146.520 MHz again.
Two handhelds are both set to 146.520 MHz, and neither is using a relay. What kind of contact is that?
tasks.success: That is simplex. Both radios use the same frequency.
tasks.hint: Simplex means the radios share one frequency. A relay is not part of this picture.

choices.label: A contact that needs a different transmit frequency

blocks.prompt: What is the difference between changing volume and changing squelch?
blocks.reference: Volume sets how loud the speaker is when the receiver is passing sound. Squelch sets how strong a signal must be before any sound is passed. Raising squelch does not make a weak signal clearer. It can hide the signal and the noise until something stronger arrives.
blocks.unsure: Go back to the squelch experiment. Open the noise, close it, then tune onto the simulated signal and watch the strength number stay independent of the squelch setting.

blocks.body: RADIO LAB PRACTICE. These questions are about the handheld you just used. They are not official exam questions.
blocks.label: RADIO LAB PRACTICE
blocks.notice: These are original Radio Lab questions about what you just did. They are not official exam questions.

questions.stem: Raising the squelch until the rushing noise stops changes which of these?
choices: How strong a signal must be before the speaker opens
How sharp the received audio becomes
The frequency the radio is tuned to
The distance a transmission will travel
questions.why: Squelch is a gate. It does not make a weak signal clearer, and it does not change the frequency. It holds the speaker closed until something meets the setting.

questions.stem: Two radios are both set to 146.520 MHz. Neither uses a relay. What is that contact?
choices: Each radio transmits on a different frequency than it receives
A contact that requires a hilltop station in the middle
Simplex
A memory channel with nothing stored
questions.why: Simplex means the radios listen and talk on the same frequency. A different transmit frequency, or a station in the middle, is a different arrangement.

questions.stem: The display changes from 145.000 MHz to 146.520 MHz. Volume and squelch stay where they were. What changed?
choices: How loud the speaker is
The frequency the radio is set to
Whether the squelch gate is open
The stored contents of every memory
questions.why: The display is the frequency the radio is set to. Volume and squelch were not the controls you moved.

questions.stem: The radio is in VFO mode and you press a tune button. What are you changing?
choices: The frequency you are tuning freely
A frequency already stored in memory
The squelch threshold
Which license you hold
questions.why: VFO is the free dial. Tuning it does not rewrite a memory, move the squelch, or change a license. Memory recall is a different control.

questions.stem: You store 146.520 MHz, tune the VFO to 146.620 MHz, then recall that memory. What does the display show?
choices: 146.620 MHz, because the last tune always wins
A blank display, because tuning erases memories
The squelch setting, instead of a frequency
questions.why: A memory keeps the frequency you stored. Tuning the VFO away does not erase it. Recall brings the stored frequency back.

blocks.prompt: You are at a trailhead for a later hilltop outing. Your friend says, "We're using 146.520 MHz simplex." Set this handheld so you could listen on that frequency. No relay is involved.
